findings.title: SESSION_SECRET placeholder not enforced in production
findings.description: The session secret defaults to a dev value with a comment saying 'change-in-prod', but there is no check to prevent it from being used in production. If deployed with the default secret, session tokens can be forged. Production deployments must use a strong random secret via environment variable, and the code should error on startup if running in production with the default.

findings.title: No HTTPS enforcement on server
findings.description: The server does not enforce HTTPS or redirect HTTP to HTTPS. Session cookies are marked secure only when NODE_ENV='production', but the server itself accepts unencrypted HTTP requests. Credentials transmitted over HTTP are trivially intercepted. Add middleware to reject or redirect HTTP in production.

findings.title: Startup migration silently claims unowned data without consent
findings.description: The runStartupMigration() function automatically links all unowned members/goals to the first user who signs up, without notifying them. If deployed with demo data, the first real user will own Rajesh Kumar, Sunita Kumar, and other test records without being asked. This is confusing and raises privacy concerns. Make the migration explicit: prompt during signup or on first login to ask if the user wants to claim existing records.

findings.title: Weak password minimum (6 characters)
findings.description: The password validation accepts 6 characters as minimum, which is below OWASP recommendations (12+). 6-character passwords are vulnerable to brute force attacks. Require at least 12 characters and add strength guidance on the signup form.

findings.title: LIMIT parameter in /api/history may not be validated
findings.description: The /api/history endpoint constructs the LIMIT clause dynamically using parseInt(req.query.limit). If parseInt fails, it returns NaN, potentially breaking the query. Validate limit explicitly: ensure it is a positive integer between 1 and a max (e.g., 1000), then use parameterized query or whitelist.

findings.title: No automated test coverage for auth flows
findings.description: There are no tests for signup, login, logout, data isolation, or ownership checks. For a beta release, add tests for: invalid email/password, duplicate signup, cross-user access (should be blocked), session expiry, and password handling.

findings.title: No security messaging or password strength guidance
findings.description: The auth UI shows no guidance about password strength, browser security, or HTTPS. Add messaging on signup about password requirements and best practices (e.g., 'Never share your password', 'Clear browser cache on shared devices').

findings.title: No password reset flow
findings.description: If a user forgets their password, they cannot recover their account. Add a password reset flow (email-based), or document that password recovery requires admin intervention.

findings.title: No email verification on signup
findings.description: Users can sign up with any email address without verification. A user could typo their email and lock themselves out of recovery. Consider adding email verification: generate a token, send a verification link, and mark the account as verified only after clicking it.
